headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates large energy users, primarily data centers, to bear the costs of their own grid infrastructure, preventing these expenses from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor's administration, some state lawmakers.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia orders data centers to pay for new transmission infrastructure
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission (SCC) has ordered data centers to cover the costs of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their facilities, preventing these expenses from being spread across other ratepayers. The governor's administration supported this change, stating it could save Virginia families and businesses hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/potential scrutiny).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: Virginia's General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, including potable and reclaimed water. This legislation aims to provide better data for understanding the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources, especially as data centers can use millions of gallons daily for cooling.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill grants localities more authority over data center siting and requires site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law Requires Noise Studies
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers to conduct site assessments examining the sound profile of new high energy use facilities, like data centers, on residential units and schools within 500 feet. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks.
